questions.question:
Let \(P(S)\) denote the power set of \(S=\{1,2,3, \ldots, 10\}\). Define the relations \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) on \(P(S)\) as \(A R_1 B\) if \(\left(A \cap B^c\right) \cup\left(B \cap A^c\right)=\phi\) and \(A R_2 B\) if \(A \cup B^c=\) \(B \cup A^c, \forall A, B \in P(S)\). Then: 

 

[JEE Main 2023, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For \(R_1,\left(A \cap B^c\right) \cup\left(B \cap A^c\right)=\phi\) means

\(A \cap B^c=\phi\) and \(B \cap A^c=\phi\),

so \(A \subseteq B\) and \(B \subseteq A\),

hence \(A=B\).

Therefore \(R_1\) is just equality on \(P(S)\),

so it is an equivalence relation.

For \(R_2, A \cup B^c=B \cup A^c\).

Taking complement on both sides, \(\left(A \cup B^c\right)^c=\left(B \cup A^c\right)^c\),

so \(A^c \cap B= B^c \cap A\).

But \(A^c \cap B=B-A\) and \(B^c \cap A=A-B\),

hence \(B-A=A-B\).

These two sets are disjoint, so they can be equal only when both are \(\phi\).

Thus \(A-B=\phi\) and \(B-A=\phi\), which gives \(A=B\).

Therefore \(R_2\) is also equality on \(P(S)\), so it is an equivalence relation.

questions.question:
The total number of six digit numbers, formed using the digits \(4,5,9\) only and divisible by 6 , is_______

 

[JEE Main 2023, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
A number divisible by \(6\) must be divisible by both \(2\) and \(3\).

Among the allowed digits \(4,5,9\), only \(4\) is even.

Therefore, the last digit must be \(4\).

Modulo \(3\), we have \(4\equiv1\), \(5\equiv2\) and \(9\equiv0\).

Since the last digit contributes residue \(1\), the sum of the residues of the first five digits must be \(2\) modulo \(3\).

Choose the first four digits freely in \(3^4\) ways.

After the first four digits are fixed, their residue sum modulo \(3\) is known.

Among \(4,5,9\), exactly one digit has the residue needed to make the sum of the first five digits congruent to \(2\) modulo \(3\).

Therefore, the fifth digit is uniquely determined for each choice of the first four digits.

Hence, the number of valid six-digit numbers is \(3^4=81\).

Therefore, the required answer is \(81\).

questions.question:
The sum of the common terms of the following three arithmetic progressions:
\(3,7,11,15, \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots, 399\),

\(2,5,8,11, \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots .359\) and

\(2,7,12,17, \ldots \ldots, 197\), is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2023, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The first A.P. is \(3,7,11,15,\ldots,399\), so its common difference is \(4\).

The second A.P. is \(2,5,8,11,\ldots,359\), so its common difference is \(3\).

The first common term of these two A.P.s is \(11\).

The common difference of their common terms is \(\operatorname{LCM}(4,3)=12\).

So, the common terms of the first two A.P.s are

\(11,23,35,47,59,\ldots\)

The third A.P. is \(2,7,12,17,\ldots,197\), so its common difference is \(5\).

Now, the first common term of \(11,23,35,47,59,\ldots\) and \(2,7,12,17,\ldots,197\) is \(47\).

The common difference of their common terms is \(\operatorname{LCM}(12,5)=60\).

So, the common terms of all three A.P.s are

\(47,107,167\)

The next term would be \(227\), which is greater than \(197\), so it is not allowed.

Therefore, the required sum is

\(47+107+167=321\)

Hence, the sum of the common terms is \(321\).

questions.question:
If the \(x\)-intercept of a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=8 x+4 y+4\) is 3 , then the length of this chord is equal to_______

[JEE Main 2023, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The parabola is

\(y^2=8x+4y+4\)

\(y^2-4y+4=8x+8\)

\((y-2)^2=8(x+1)\)

Use shifted coordinates \(X=x+1\) and \(Y=y-2\).

Then the parabola is \(Y^2=8X\), with focus \((2,0)\) in shifted coordinates.

The focal chord has \(x\)-intercept \(3\), which is the point \((3,0)\) in original coordinates or \((4,-2)\) in shifted coordinates.

The line through \((2,0)\) and \((4,-2)\) is \(Y=2-X\).

At its intersections with the parabola,

\((2-X)^2=8X\)

\(X^2-12X+4=0\)

The difference of the roots is

\(|X_1-X_2|=\sqrt{12^2-4(1)(4)}=8\sqrt{2}\)

\(\because Y=2-X\), \(|Y_1-Y_2|=|X_1-X_2|=8\sqrt{2}\)

The chord length is

\(\sqrt{(8\sqrt{2})^2+(8\sqrt{2})^2}=16\)

\(\therefore\) the required length is \(16\).
